pr.title: Refactor numeric feature centering
pr.body: center(train, test): train is nonempty; subtract the training mean from both lists without fitting on test data.

head_files.module.py:
def center(train, test):
    fitting_values = train + test
    offset = sum(fitting_values) / len(fitting_values)
    return [value - offset for value in train], [value - offset for value in test]

changed_files.patch:
--- a/module.py
+++ b/module.py
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
 def center(train, test):
-    mean = sum(train) / len(train)
-    return [x - mean for x in train], [x - mean for x in test]
+    fitting_values = train + test
+    offset = sum(fitting_values) / len(fitting_values)
+    return [value - offset for value in train], [value - offset for value in test]

gold_issues.description: Fitting the centering offset on train plus test leaks held-out information into training features.

findings.description: The refactor calculates the mean using both training and test data, violating the requirement to only fit on training data, leading to incorrect centering of the test data.

input.body: The refactor introduces a defect in the `center` function. The new implementation calculates the mean using both `train` and `test` data, which violates the requirement to only fit on the training data. This leads to incorrect centering of the test data based on the combined mean, which can result in misleading results when evaluating models. Specifically, the test data should not influence the mean calculation. Please revert to the original implementation that calculates the mean solely from the training data.
